papers_read.title_as_printed: Transfer learning for predicting conversion from mild cognitive impairment to dementia of Alzheimer's type based on a three-dimensional convolutional neural network (Bae et al., Neurobiology of Aging 99 (2021) 53-64)
An end-to-end multimodal 3D CNN framework with multi-level features for the prediction of mild cognitive impairment (Zhang et al., Knowledge-Based Systems 281 (2023) 111064)

what_each_reports.P-37: ResNet29 3D CNN on whole-brain baseline sMRI, pretrained on NC vs DAT (transfer learning), ADNI; 228 MCI converters within 3 years vs 222 MCI non-converters who remained MCI for at least 3 years (shorter-follow-up non-converters excluded); single 70/15/15 split, 68 test scans: accuracy 82.4% (56/68 correct across 1.5T and 3T), AUC 0.827, EER 0.189.
what_each_reports.P-72: Twin 3D ResNet18 on sMRI grey matter + FDG-PET, ADNI (151 pMCI converting within 3 years, 238 sMCI 'did not convert'), 70/15/15 split averaged over three test subsets. AD vs NC accuracy 94.61%; sMCI vs pMCI accuracy 77.19% (AUC 0.755). Its sMRI-only MAResNet18 gives 73.68% for sMCI vs pMCI.

quantity_a: Held-out accuracy (68 test scans) for MCI-to-DAT conversion within 3 years vs MCI stable for at least 3 years, ADNI, whole-brain structural MRI only.
quantity_b: As recorded: 94.61%, which is P-72's AD vs NC diagnostic accuracy (sMRI+PET), not a conversion result. P-72's conversion figure is 77.19% (sMRI+PET) or 73.68% (sMRI only).
incompatible_if_same: No. As recorded the numbers are on different tasks. On the conversion task, P-37's 82.4% (56/68; Wilson 95% interval roughly 72-90%) contains P-72's sMRI-only 73.68% and multimodal 77.19%, and neither paper claims the other's method fails on the same data.

gates.task: mismatch as recorded (T2 conversion vs AD-vs-NC diagnosis); match (T2, 3-year horizon) only if P-72's 77.19%/73.68% is substituted, and even then P-37 excludes non-converters followed for under 3 years while P-72 does not state that restriction.
gates.validation_tier: match in tier: internal held-out splits in both (P-37 one split of 68; P-72 three splits averaged).
gates.modality_family: mismatch for P-72's reported model: P-72 fuses sMRI with FDG-PET; P-37 uses sMRI only. The record's 'structural_mri' for both is wrong.

endpoint_and_metric: incompatible as recorded (conversion endpoint vs AD-vs-NC diagnosis); both are accuracy.
performance_validity: flag does not apply: 82.4% and 94.61% are below 0.97.
independence: Distinct studies and author groups; both draw on ADNI MCI participants, so overlap is likely but not disqualifying.
grounds: The record misreads P-72: 94.61% is its AD-vs-NC accuracy, and its sMCI-vs-pMCI accuracy is 77.19%.
On the conversion task the two results overlap: P-37's 82.4% on 68 test scans cannot exclude P-72's 77.19% (or its sMRI-only 73.68%).
Neither paper claims an ordering the other refutes; each reports its own model's score on its own ADNI selection.

record_defects: claim_b '94.61% AD on T2' is P-72's AD vs NC accuracy; P-72's T2 accuracy is 77.19%. task_equal 'Yes' is wrong as recorded.
modality_family 'structural_mri' is wrong for P-72, which fuses sMRI grey matter with FDG-PET.
The rejection reason 'Metric type unclear: Acc / Unknown' is wrong: 94.61% is an accuracy.
The bridging-evidence list names no separating condition; 'partially resolved' is unsupported.
what_would_change_the_verdict: Nothing in these two papers; a like-for-like sMRI-only conversion comparison whose intervals did not overlap, with matching stable-MCI definitions, would be needed.
